correctness.rationale: For Haar probability on the ordinary four-torus, the 36 ordered two-edge pairs have 6 singleton, 12 double and 1 six-element sum fibers. The latter consists of the three perfect matchings with both orderings. Thus the unweighted witness gives (6+48+36)/36=5/2. For arbitrary complex coefficients Parseval gives 2S²−sum |a|⁴ plus eight times the real part of the three distinct cross products of matching products. Grouping squared magnitudes into matching masses b_j gives the upper bound 3S²−(3/2) sum b_j². Equality requires all three masses equal, equality within each pair of magnitudes, and all three matching products aligned. Since S>0, their products then agree and the phase factorization follows by choosing a unit square root of a_12 a_13/a_23 after normalizing magnitudes. The converse is immediate. This checks the unrestricted-complex statement, not only the finite count. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed; no formal verification or external attestation is inferred.
